what_it_is: The liver is the largest organ inside the body. It cleans the blood, makes important proteins, makes bile to digest fat, and stores energy, vitamins and minerals.
why_it_matters: Many liver tests check one of these jobs. Knowing the jobs helps explain why each test is ordered.
if_higher_or_worse: When the liver is damaged for a long time, it can slowly lose the ability to do these jobs.
if_lower_or_better: The liver can repair itself, especially in early disease, if the cause of damage is reduced.

what_it_is: Some blood tests show liver irritation (ALT, AST). Others show how well the liver is working (albumin, bilirubin, INR, platelets).
why_it_matters: ALT and AST are often called liver function tests, but they measure irritation, not how well the liver works.
if_higher_or_worse: Falling albumin, or rising bilirubin or INR, usually says more about how well the liver works than a high ALT alone.
if_lower_or_better: A normal or falling ALT does not by itself mean the liver works normally. Function tests and scans give the fuller picture.

what_it_is: The liver cleans your blood. It removes waste and breaks down medicines.
why_it_matters: If the liver gets weak, waste and medicines stay in the body longer.
if_higher_or_worse: In a very sick liver, waste can build up and cause confusion.
if_lower_or_better: A healthy liver cleans the blood on time.

what_it_is: The liver makes albumin, which holds fluid inside blood vessels, and clotting factors, which help blood clot.
why_it_matters: Albumin and INR are the main blood tests for this job.
if_higher_or_worse: When this job weakens, albumin falls (fluid can leak into the legs or belly) and INR rises (bruising or bleeding happens more easily).
if_lower_or_better: Normal albumin and INR suggest the liver is making enough of these proteins.

what_it_is: The liver makes bile, a fluid that helps digest fat. It also clears bilirubin, a yellow substance from old red blood cells, into the bile.
why_it_matters: Bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and GGT are the main tests for this job.
if_higher_or_worse: When bile does not flow well or the liver cannot clear bilirubin, the skin and eyes can turn yellow (jaundice), urine can darken and the skin can itch.
if_lower_or_better: Normal bilirubin means the liver is clearing this substance as expected.

what_it_is: The liver stores sugar and lets it out between meals to keep your blood sugar steady.
why_it_matters: Fatty liver and diabetes often go together.
if_higher_or_worse: High blood sugar can put more fat in the liver.
if_lower_or_better: Better blood sugar (a lower A1c) helps the liver.

what_it_is: The liver handles fat from food and makes cholesterol. In fatty liver, extra fat gets stored in the liver.
why_it_matters: A FibroScan CAP number shows how much fat is there.
if_higher_or_worse: More fat can lead to irritation and, over time, scars.
if_lower_or_better: Losing weight slowly and moving more can lower liver fat.

what_it_is: The liver stores vitamins, like A, D and B12, and minerals, like iron.
why_it_matters: A very sick liver may not store enough, so some vitamins can run low.
if_higher_or_worse: Low vitamins can affect bones and energy.
if_lower_or_better: Your care team will check and suggest vitamins only if you need them.

what_it_is: The liver helps filter bacteria that come from the gut into the blood.
why_it_matters: People with cirrhosis have a higher risk of infections.
if_higher_or_worse: Fever, belly pain or confusion in someone with cirrhosis can be a sign of infection and needs prompt medical attention.
if_lower_or_better: Keeping vaccines up to date helps protect the liver.

what_it_is: A condition where extra fat builds up in the liver, linked to weight, blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol. The older name was NAFLD.
why_it_matters: It is the most common liver disease. Most people feel no symptoms, so tests are the main way to follow it.
if_higher_or_worse: If fat leads to irritation and scarring over years, it can progress toward cirrhosis.
if_lower_or_better: Gradual weight loss, regular activity and good control of diabetes and cholesterol can reduce liver fat.

what_it_is: Fatty liver with irritation and damage to liver cells. The old name was NASH.
why_it_matters: The irritation is what slowly causes scars.
if_higher_or_worse: If the irritation goes on for years, scars can build up.
if_lower_or_better: The irritation can go away with weight loss and better blood sugar.

what_it_is: Scar tissue in the liver. It is staged from F0 (no scarring) to F4 (cirrhosis).
why_it_matters: The stage of scarring is the strongest guide to long-term liver health.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher stages (F3, F4) mean more scarring and need closer follow-up.
if_lower_or_better: Early scarring can improve when the cause of liver damage is reduced.

what_it_is: Heavy scarring of the liver. The scars change the liver's shape and can stop it from working well.
why_it_matters: People with cirrhosis need regular check-ups and cancer screening.
if_higher_or_worse: Cirrhosis can cause fluid in the belly, bleeding, confusion and liver cancer.
if_lower_or_better: Many people with cirrhosis stay stable for years with good care.

what_it_is: Compensated means the liver is scarred but still doing its job. Decompensated means problems have started, like fluid in the belly, bleeding, confusion or yellow skin.
why_it_matters: It changes how often you see your doctor and what care you need.
if_higher_or_worse: Going from compensated to decompensated is a big change that needs close care.
if_lower_or_better: Staying compensated is a main goal.

what_it_is: A group of problems that often come together: extra belly weight, high blood sugar, high blood pressure and high blood fats.
why_it_matters: These problems cause fatty liver and raise the chance of heart disease.
if_higher_or_worse: The more of these you have, the higher the risk.
if_lower_or_better: Improving even one of them helps your liver and heart.

what_it_is: The most common type of cancer that starts in the liver. People with cirrhosis have a higher risk.
why_it_matters: Screening every 6 months with ultrasound, often with an AFP blood test, aims to find it early.
if_higher_or_worse: Missing screening can delay finding cancer at a treatable stage.
if_lower_or_better: Keeping up with screening is the best protection.

what_it_is: A blood sample measured in a lab. Each result is compared with a reference range, the usual range for healthy people at that lab.
why_it_matters: Ranges differ slightly between labs, so always read the range printed on your own report.
if_higher_or_worse: An (H) next to a result means it is above the lab's range.
if_lower_or_better: An (L) means it is below the range. Slightly out of range is common and not always a problem.

what_it_is: Marks on a lab report showing a result above (H) or below (L) the lab's reference range.
why_it_matters: Flags help spot results to discuss, but one flagged value is often less important than the trend over time.
if_higher_or_worse: (H) means higher than the usual range.
if_lower_or_better: (L) means lower than the usual range.

what_it_is: A blood test number. ALT is a substance inside liver cells. It spills into the blood when the liver is irritated.
why_it_matters: It shows if something is bothering the liver, like extra fat, alcohol or some medicines.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher ALT usually means the liver is more irritated.
if_lower_or_better: Lower ALT often means less irritation. But ALT can be normal even when there is fat or scarring.
related_terms: What does it mean if my ALT goes down?

what_it_is: A substance found in the liver and also in muscle and heart. It rises when these tissues are hurt.
why_it_matters: AST is read together with ALT. It is also part of the FIB-4 score.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher AST can mean liver damage. AST higher than ALT can be seen with alcohol-related damage or more advanced scarring.
if_lower_or_better: Falling AST often means less damage, with the same caution as ALT: normal does not rule out liver disease.

what_it_is: A substance found in the bile ducts of the liver and in bone.
why_it_matters: ALP helps check whether bile is flowing normally.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher ALP can mean a problem with bile flow, such as PBC, PSC or a blockage, or can come from bone.
if_lower_or_better: A low ALP is rarely a concern.

what_it_is: A substance found mainly in the liver's bile ducts.
why_it_matters: GGT helps show whether a high ALP comes from the liver. It can also rise with alcohol use and some medicines.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher GGT can mean bile duct irritation, alcohol use or medicine effects.
if_lower_or_better: Falling GGT can follow reduced alcohol or improved bile flow.

what_it_is: A yellow substance made when old red blood cells break down. The liver clears it into bile.
why_it_matters: Bilirubin shows how well the liver clears this substance. It is part of the MELD score.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher bilirubin can mean the liver is not clearing it well, bile flow is blocked, or red cells are breaking down faster. Very high levels cause jaundice. A harmless inherited condition (Gilbert syndrome) can also raise it.
if_lower_or_better: Lower or normal bilirubin is expected and not a concern.

what_it_is: The main protein in blood, made by the liver. It keeps fluid inside blood vessels.
why_it_matters: Albumin is one of the best blood signs of how well the liver makes proteins. It is part of MELD 3.0.
if_higher_or_worse: A high albumin is uncommon and usually reflects dehydration.
if_lower_or_better: Lower albumin can mean the liver is making less protein, poor nutrition, or protein loss through the kidneys. Low albumin can lead to swelling and fluid in the belly.

what_it_is: A test of how long blood takes to clot. The liver makes most clotting factors.
why_it_matters: INR shows how well the liver makes clotting proteins. It is part of the MELD score.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher INR means blood takes longer to clot, which can mean the liver makes fewer clotting factors. Blood thinners such as warfarin and low vitamin K also raise it.
if_lower_or_better: An INR in the normal range means clotting time is as expected.

what_it_is: Small cell fragments in blood that help it clot.
why_it_matters: In liver scarring, the spleen can enlarge and trap platelets, so a falling platelet count can be a sign scarring is advancing. Platelets are part of FIB-4.
if_higher_or_worse: A high platelet count has other causes such as irritation or low iron.
if_lower_or_better: Lower platelets can mean advancing scarring with an enlarged spleen, or other causes. Very low counts raise bleeding risk.
related_terms: What does it mean if my platelets go down?

what_it_is: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
why_it_matters: A low level (anemia) can cause tiredness and can be a sign of bleeding.
if_higher_or_worse: High hemoglobin can come from dehydration, smoking or other conditions.
if_lower_or_better: A sudden drop can be a sign of bleeding, especially with black stool or vomiting blood, and needs urgent care.

what_it_is: A waste product filtered by the kidneys.
why_it_matters: It shows kidney function, which can be affected in cirrhosis and by diuretics. It is part of the MELD score.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher creatinine means the kidneys are filtering less, for example from dehydration, medicines such as NSAIDs or kidney strain.
if_lower_or_better: Lower or normal creatinine usually means kidneys are filtering well.

what_it_is: The level of salt in the blood. This is different from the salt you eat.
why_it_matters: Low blood sodium is common in advanced cirrhosis with fluid buildup. It is part of MELD.
if_higher_or_worse: High blood sodium usually reflects dehydration.
if_lower_or_better: Low blood sodium can cause tiredness or confusion. It does not mean you should eat more salt: a low-salt diet may still be recommended.

what_it_is: A number that shows how well your kidneys clean your blood.
why_it_matters: It helps your doctor choose safe medicines and doses.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: A lower number means the kidneys are cleaning less.

what_it_is: A blood test showing average blood sugar over about the past 3 months.
why_it_matters: Diabetes and fatty liver make each other worse, so blood sugar control is part of liver care.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher A1c means blood sugar has been higher on average.
if_lower_or_better: Lower A1c means better average blood sugar control, which helps the liver.

what_it_is: The amount of sugar in the blood at the time of the test.
why_it_matters: A single glucose value depends on recent meals; A1c shows the longer trend.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher glucose can mean diabetes or recent eating.
if_lower_or_better: Very low glucose can cause shakiness or confusion and needs prompt treatment.

what_it_is: Fats in your blood. LDL is the bad kind. HDL is the good kind. Triglycerides are another kind of blood fat.
why_it_matters: People with fatty liver often have high blood fats and a higher chance of heart disease.
if_higher_or_worse: High LDL and triglycerides raise heart risk.
if_lower_or_better: Lower LDL and triglycerides, and higher HDL, are better for your heart.

what_it_is: A protein measured in blood, used with ultrasound to screen for liver cancer in people with cirrhosis.
why_it_matters: It is one part of 6-month liver cancer screening.
if_higher_or_worse: A higher AFP needs follow-up but has several possible causes, not only cancer.
if_lower_or_better: A normal AFP is reassuring but does not rule out cancer, which is why the ultrasound is also done.

what_it_is: A score calculated from age, AST, ALT and platelets that estimates the chance of significant liver scarring.
why_it_matters: It is a quick first check that helps decide who needs a FibroScan or other tests.
if_higher_or_worse: A higher score (commonly above 2.67) suggests a higher chance of advanced scarring and usually leads to more testing.
if_lower_or_better: A lower score (commonly below 1.3) suggests advanced scarring is unlikely. Cutoffs differ for people over 65.

what_it_is: A score for cirrhosis severity calculated from bilirubin, INR, creatinine, sodium, albumin and sex. Scores range from 6 to 40. MELD-Na is the older version.
why_it_matters: It helps the care team judge how advanced cirrhosis is and is used for liver transplant priority.
if_higher_or_worse: A higher or rising MELD means more severe liver disease and needs closer attention.
if_lower_or_better: A lower score means less severe disease. A score near 6 to 9 is at the low end.
related_terms: What does it mean if my MELD goes up?

what_it_is: A number calculated from weight and height.
why_it_matters: It is a rough guide to weight-related health risk, including fatty liver.
if_higher_or_worse: A higher BMI is linked with more liver fat.
if_lower_or_better: Gradual weight loss that lowers BMI can reduce liver fat.

what_it_is: A painless ultrasound-based test that measures liver stiffness (in kPa, a sign of scarring) and liver fat (CAP score, in dB/m).
why_it_matters: It tracks scarring and fat without a needle.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher stiffness suggests more scarring; irritation or eating before the test can also raise it. A higher CAP means more fat.
if_lower_or_better: Lower stiffness or CAP over time can mean less scarring or fat.
related_terms: What does it mean if my FibroScan stiffness goes down?

what_it_is: A painless scan using sound waves to look at the liver.
why_it_matters: For people with cirrhosis, ultrasound every 6 months, often with AFP, screens for liver cancer.
if_higher_or_worse: A new spot on the liver needs follow-up testing, often with MRI or CT.
if_lower_or_better: A scan without new findings is reassuring; screening continues every 6 months.

what_it_is: A procedure where a thin camera is passed through the mouth to look at the esophagus, stomach and first part of the intestine.
why_it_matters: In cirrhosis it checks for swollen veins (varices) that could bleed.
if_higher_or_worse: Larger varices may need treatment to prevent bleeding.
if_lower_or_better: Small or no varices usually means repeat checks at set intervals.

what_it_is: A doctor takes a tiny piece of the liver with a needle to look at under a microscope.
why_it_matters: It shows fat, irritation and scarring directly.
if_higher_or_worse: The results tell the scarring stage.
if_lower_or_better: Today, many people get a FibroScan instead.

what_it_is: Swollen veins in the esophagus or stomach caused by high pressure in liver blood flow in cirrhosis.
why_it_matters: They can bleed, which is an emergency.
if_higher_or_worse: Larger varices have a higher bleeding risk and may need medicine or banding.
if_lower_or_better: Small varices are watched with repeat EGD.

what_it_is: Bleeding in the digestive tract. Signs include vomiting blood or coffee-ground material, and black, tarry or bloody stool.
why_it_matters: In cirrhosis, bleeding can be life-threatening. SEEK URGENT CARE OR CALL 911 if these signs appear.
if_higher_or_worse: Any of these signs needs emergency care right away.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Fluid that collects in the belly in advanced cirrhosis.
why_it_matters: It shows the liver disease is affecting fluid balance; it is treated with a low-salt diet and diuretics.
if_higher_or_worse: A growing belly or quick weight gain over days can mean more fluid and should be reported.
if_lower_or_better: Less swelling and stable weight suggest fluid is controlled.

what_it_is: Swelling, usually in the feet, ankles and legs, from extra fluid. LE means lower extremity.
why_it_matters: It often comes with low albumin or fluid buildup in cirrhosis.
if_higher_or_worse: Worsening swelling should be reported to the care team.
if_lower_or_better: Less swelling suggests better fluid control.

what_it_is: Confusion caused by a very sick liver. When the liver can't clean the blood, waste builds up and affects the brain.
why_it_matters: It can start small: poor sleep, forgetting things, or acting different.
if_higher_or_worse: New or worse confusion is an emergency. Get help right away.
if_lower_or_better: With treatment, many people stay clear-headed.

what_it_is: Yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes from high bilirubin.
why_it_matters: New jaundice should be reported to the care team promptly.
if_higher_or_worse: Deepening yellow color, dark urine or pale stool should be reported.
if_lower_or_better: Normal skin and eye color is expected.

what_it_is: High blood pressure in the vein that carries blood from the gut to the liver, caused by scarring.
why_it_matters: It explains varices, an enlarged spleen, low platelets and ascites.
if_higher_or_worse: Signs of worsening include falling platelets, new varices or fluid buildup.
if_lower_or_better: Stable platelets and no new complications suggest it is stable.

what_it_is: Pain relievers such as ibuprofen, naproxen and diclofenac.
why_it_matters: In cirrhosis they can harm the kidneys, raise bleeding risk and worsen fluid buildup, so plans often say no NSAIDs.
if_higher_or_worse: Using NSAIDs with cirrhosis raises the risk of kidney and bleeding problems.
if_lower_or_better: If an NSAID is on your list and your plan says to avoid them, ask your care team before stopping or taking it.

what_it_is: A pain and fever reliever.
why_it_matters: It is often the preferred pain reliever in liver disease, but only up to the daily limit your care team sets, which may be lower than the package maximum.
if_higher_or_worse: Taking more than the limit, or with alcohol, can injure the liver.
if_lower_or_better: Staying within your set limit is the safe approach. Check other products for hidden acetaminophen.

what_it_is: Medicines that help the body remove extra fluid through urine.
why_it_matters: They treat ascites and leg swelling. Blood tests check kidneys and salts while taking them.
if_higher_or_worse: Too much fluid loss can cause dizziness or kidney strain; report these.
if_lower_or_better: Stable weight and less swelling suggest they are working.

what_it_is: Products like herbs, teas, pills and powders you can buy without a prescription.
why_it_matters: Some of them can hurt the liver, even ones called natural.
if_higher_or_worse: A new supplement can sometimes harm the liver.
if_lower_or_better: Tell your care team about every supplement you take.

what_it_is: The part of the note describing why you came and how you have been.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Your past and current medical conditions.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: A checklist of symptoms the doctor asked about.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: The doctor's summary and the plan for each problem. Usually the most useful part for patients.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Years old, for example 53 y/o.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: After a procedure, for example s/p liver biopsy.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: A past condition, for example h/o gallstones.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Take only when needed.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Take two times a day.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Repeat every 6 months, for example imaging q6 months.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Alcohol, for example avoid EtOH.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: The legs, for example LE edema means leg swelling.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Swollen lymph nodes; no LAD means none were found.
why_it_matters: Notes use shorthand to save time; Model A explains it in plain words.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: The number of steps your watch counts each day.
why_it_matters: Physical activity is part of treating fatty liver. Steps show whether activity is changing between visits.
if_higher_or_worse: More steps toward your goal means more activity, which helps the liver and heart.
if_lower_or_better: A sudden drop in steps can happen when someone feels unwell. Tell your care team if you feel sick.

what_it_is: A common goal: about 150 minutes of brisk walking or similar activity each week. That is about 30 minutes, 5 days a week.
why_it_matters: Moving more can lower liver fat. Even 10-minute walks count.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Your heart rate while at rest, measured by your watch.
why_it_matters: It can reflect fitness, sleep, illness or medicines.
if_higher_or_worse: A resting heart rate that stays higher than usual can follow illness, poor sleep or dehydration.
if_lower_or_better: A lower resting heart rate over time often reflects better fitness.

what_it_is: Slowly losing weight, often about 0.5 to 2 pounds a week.
why_it_matters: Weight loss is a main treatment for fatty liver; larger losses (often around 7 to 10% of body weight) are linked with less fat, irritation and scarring.
if_higher_or_worse: Quick weight GAIN over a few days in cirrhosis can mean fluid buildup and should be reported.
if_lower_or_better: Steady gradual loss is the goal; crash diets are not recommended.
related_terms: What does it mean if my weight goes up quickly?

what_it_is: Eating no more than about 2,000 mg (2 grams) of sodium a day.
why_it_matters: In cirrhosis with fluid buildup, less salt helps control ascites and swelling.
if_higher_or_worse: Salty foods can worsen fluid buildup.
if_lower_or_better: Reading food labels and limiting processed food helps stay under the limit.

what_it_is: Your liver has to break down every drink of alcohol. Alcohol can hurt the liver.
why_it_matters: If you have fatty liver or cirrhosis, your care team will likely ask you to drink less or stop.
if_higher_or_worse: Drinking can make scarring worse, faster.
if_lower_or_better: Drinking less or stopping helps the liver heal.

term: What does it mean if my ALT goes down?
what_it_is: ALT is a number from a blood test. It goes up when the liver is irritated.
why_it_matters: When ALT goes down, the liver is often less irritated. This can happen after losing weight, moving more or drinking less alcohol.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: This is usually good news. But a normal ALT does not always mean a healthy liver. Your doctor also looks at other tests, like platelets and FibroScan.

term: What does it mean if my ALT goes up?
what_it_is: ALT goes up when the liver is more irritated.
why_it_matters: Common reasons: more liver fat, alcohol, a new medicine or supplement, an infection, or hard exercise.
if_higher_or_worse: Talk with your care team about any recent changes.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

term: What does it mean if my platelets go down?
what_it_is: Platelets help blood clot.
why_it_matters: In liver disease, a falling count over time can be a sign scarring is advancing and the spleen is trapping platelets.
if_higher_or_worse: A steady fall is worth discussing; very low counts raise bleeding risk.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

term: What does it mean if my bilirubin goes up?
what_it_is: Bilirubin is a yellow substance the liver clears out.
why_it_matters: When it goes up, the liver may not be clearing it well. In cirrhosis, this is important to report.
if_higher_or_worse: Tell your care team soon, especially if your skin or eyes look yellow or your pee is dark.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

term: What does it mean if my albumin goes down?
what_it_is: Albumin is a protein made by the liver.
why_it_matters: A fall can mean the liver is making less protein or nutrition is poor, and can lead to swelling.
if_higher_or_worse: Falling albumin is worth discussing, especially with new swelling.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

term: What does it mean if my MELD goes up?
what_it_is: MELD is a cirrhosis severity score.
why_it_matters: A rising MELD means the liver disease is more severe than before.
if_higher_or_worse: A rise of several points between visits needs your care team's attention.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

term: What does it mean if my A1c goes down?
what_it_is: A1c shows average blood sugar over about 3 months.
why_it_matters: A falling A1c means better blood sugar control, which helps reduce liver fat.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Usually a good sign. Very fast drops with dizziness or shakiness should be reported, as blood sugar may be going too low.

term: What does it mean if my FibroScan stiffness goes down?
what_it_is: Liver stiffness on FibroScan reflects scarring.
why_it_matters: A lower reading over time can mean less scarring or less irritation.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Often a good sign, but readings vary with eating and irritation, so trends over more than one test matter most.

term: What does it mean if my weight goes up quickly?
what_it_is: Weight measured on a scale each day.
why_it_matters: In cirrhosis, gaining about 2 kg (around 4 to 5 pounds) or more over a few days can mean fluid is building up.
if_higher_or_worse: Quick weight gain, a growing belly or more leg swelling should be reported to your care team.
if_lower_or_better: Not applicable.

what_it_is: Think of fatty liver disease as a ladder. From top to bottom: healthy liver, fatty liver, fatty liver with irritation (MASH), scarring (F1 to F3), and cirrhosis (F4).
why_it_matters: Knowing your step helps you understand your care plan.
if_higher_or_worse: Moving down the ladder is slow. It often takes years and has no symptoms.
if_lower_or_better: Many people can climb back up. Fat and irritation can go away, and early scars can get better.

what_it_is: Fibrosis stage describes how much scar tissue is in the liver: F0 none, F1 mild, F2 moderate, F3 severe (advanced), F4 cirrhosis. Think of it like a scar on the skin after a deep cut, but inside the liver.
why_it_matters: The stage is the strongest guide to long-term liver health. It comes from a FibroScan, a biopsy, or blood scores such as FIB-4 that your doctor reads together.
if_higher_or_worse: F3 and F4 need closer follow-up, including cancer screening for F4.
if_lower_or_better: F0 to F2 means less scarring. Earlier stages have the best chance of improving.

what_it_is: FibroScan gives two numbers: stiffness in kPa (a sign of scarring) and CAP in dB/m (a sign of fat). Your doctor turns these into an estimated fibrosis stage and fat grade.
why_it_matters: Cutoffs differ by device, disease and clinic, so the stage your doctor writes in the note matters more than the raw number.
if_higher_or_worse: Higher stiffness suggests more scarring; higher CAP suggests more fat. Eating before the test or active irritation can raise stiffness.
if_lower_or_better: Lower numbers over repeated tests can mean less scarring or fat.

also_known_as: get back to a healthy liver
what_it_is: Yes. Fatty liver often goes away when you lose weight slowly, move more, drink less alcohol and control blood sugar.
why_it_matters: That is why your care plan focuses on daily habits.
if_higher_or_worse: Without changes, fat can lead to irritation and scars.
if_lower_or_better: Less liver fat lowers the chance of irritation and scars.
related_terms: How much weight loss helps the liver

term: Can MASH go back to simple fatty liver?
what_it_is: Often, yes. In a well-known 2015 study of 293 people with biopsy-proven NASH who changed diet and activity for one year, NASH went away in 90% of those who lost 10% or more of their weight.
why_it_matters: When irritation goes away, the main driver of new scarring is removed.
if_higher_or_worse: Ongoing irritation keeps scarring going.
if_lower_or_better: Losing more weight was linked with better results: about 64% resolution with 7 to 10% loss and 35% with 5 to 7% loss.
related_terms: How much weight loss helps the liver

what_it_is: Yes, scars can get better, especially early ones. In one large study, scars improved in almost half of people who lost 10% or more of their weight.
why_it_matters: Even if scars don't get better, stopping them from getting worse matters a lot.
if_higher_or_worse: Cirrhosis (F4) is harder to reverse, but good care can slow it down.
if_lower_or_better: Early stages (F1 and F2) have the best chance of getting better.
related_terms: How much weight loss helps the liver

term: How much weight loss helps the liver
also_known_as: how much weight should I lose
what_it_is: In the 2015 study, more weight loss meant more liver improvement. With 10% or more: MASH went away in 90% and scarring improved in 45%. With 7 to 10%: 64% and 33%. With 5 to 7%: 35% and 21%. Under 5%: 10% and 7%.
why_it_matters: Every bit of steady weight loss helps; each extra 1% was linked with a higher chance of MASH going away.
if_higher_or_worse: Fast or crash dieting is not recommended.
if_lower_or_better: Your care team will set a safe, personal goal. In cirrhosis, keeping muscle and eating enough protein also matter.
related_terms: Can MASH go back to simple fatty liver?

what_it_is: There are now two medicines for MASH in the US: Rezdiffra (since March 2024) and Wegovy (since August 2025). They are for adults with some scarring (F2 or F3), not cirrhosis.
why_it_matters: They work best together with healthy eating and moving more.
if_higher_or_worse: Not applicable.
if_lower_or_better: Your doctor decides if a medicine fits you. Model A does not suggest medicines.
